label: REJECT
rationale: Scorecard 47/100 — classification REJECT — with a business-quality subtotal of 41/75, far below every other name analysed in this harness (TSM 66, NVDA 62, 005930 59, AVGO 57). THE SCREENING RUN WAS WRONG ABOUT WHAT THIS COMPANY IS. The 2026-09-04 screen ranked 012450 fifth for deep work as a European-rearmament defence play uncorrelated with AI capex. The filings show that by revenue it is now 64% SHIPBUILDING — 해양 was KRW 9,614.2B of H1 2026's KRW 15,043.9B, against 방산 at 29.68% — and marine has overtaken defence on operating profit as well. Shipbuilding is a cyclical industry with a historically poor record on returns on capital, not a structural-growth industry. Correcting that misidentification is the main work of this analysis. THE DECISIVE FINDING is cash. H1 2026 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE KRW 370.7B against POSITIVE KRW 1,014.3B a year earlier — a KRW 1.39T swing — while the company reported KRW 2.00T of operating profit. Investing consumed a further KRW 3,403.0B, and total borrowings rose 24.6% in six months from KRW 12.39T to KRW 15.44T. Interest of KRW 264.7B was paid out of financing, not operations. This follows a 13.1% equity dilution in 2025 (5,982,240 new shares across a third-party placement and a rights issue). Equity raised, then debt raised, while operations consumed cash. AND THE MOAT LEG IS SHRINKING. Defence revenue fell about 14% versus the FY2025 half-year run-rate and defence margin slipped from 21.9% to 20.2%, while the lower-moat marine business grew. That is the opposite of the direction-of-change evidence the deep-analyst contract prioritises. WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD: order backlog of KRW 114.92T, about 3.8 years of revenue, with defence backlog alone at KRW 46.85T. Group operating margin expanded from 11.6% to 13.3% and marine margin from 7.7% to 12.0%. Non-controlling interests taking about 44% of profit also means the parent's economic exposure to marine is smaller than consolidated revenue implies. THE PRICE MAKES IT A REJECT RATHER THAN A WATCH. At KRW 1,244,000 the market capitalisation of about KRW 64.14T is 5.35x owners' equity of KRW 12.00T and 35.8x H1 2026 annualised owners' earnings. Reverse-engineered, even a generous 22x multiple requires owners' net income to rise about 60% and stay there; at a normal 15-18x it requires a doubling. The modelled BULL CASE returns only +9% to +40% over five years, and the probability-weighted return is approximately NEGATIVE 37% — the only negative expected return in this harness, and robust to reweighting: even at bear 0.15 / base 0.45 / bull 0.40 it stays around -18%. REJECT is a statement about the INVESTMENT AT THIS PRICE, not a judgement that the company is bad. The backlog is real and the structural driver behind the defence leg is real. But the strategy exists to find asymmetric outliers, and a distribution whose optimistic case barely beats cash while the downside is levered is the opposite of that. Note that no Hard Veto reads FAIL — the label follows the score and the negative expected return, not a veto trigger. TWO CORRECTIONS APPLIED AFTER RED-TEAM REVIEW, NEITHER OF WHICH CHANGES THE VERDICT. FIRST, the red team returned REVISE partly on the ground that FY2025 operating cash flow was sitting unextracted in a supplied document. That premise is FALSE: the [정정]영업보고서 is an image-based PDF containing no machine-readable financial statements, and the 반기보고서 carries only H1 comparatives. The number is genuinely unavailable from what was supplied — the substantive criticism (it is decisive and unknown) stands, but the analysis did not ignore data it had. The correction also revealed what the March 2026 amendment changed: 기업결합 사항, 타회사 출자현황 and the 이사회 결의서 — administrative items, not a restatement. SECOND, the leverage characterisation was too harsh. Net debt/EBITDA was 1.6x at 2025-09-30 with coverage rated excellent, implying roughly 1.2-1.3x now — conservative by any conventional standard. financial_survivability is raised 6 to 7 and the total to 48/100, still firmly in the Reject band. The genuine concern is narrower than the earlier draft implied: not debt quantum or solvency, but CASH CONVERSION — a 1.08 current ratio and negative operating cash flow while borrowings rose 24.6% in six months.
increase_evidence: PRIMARY: FY2025 and FY2026 full-year operating cash flow turning clearly positive. NOTE THIS CANNOT BE OBTAINED FROM THE DOCUMENTS SUPPLIED — the [정정]영업보고서 is image-based and the 반기보고서 carries only H1 comparatives. The FY2025 사업보고서 or audited cash flow statement is required. Without this number nothing else matters.
Defence revenue and margin re-accelerating — order intake, not just backlog — reversing the -14% revenue and 21.9%-to-20.2% margin decline.
Borrowings stabilising or falling from KRW 15.44T without a further equity raise, with the current ratio improving from 1.08.

A price decline of roughly 40-50%, which is what the normalised earnings analysis implies is required for the expectation gap to turn positive on current evidence. Per policy/position-sizing.yaml price alone is never sufficient — it must accompany at least the cash flow evidence above.
Marine margin sustaining at or above 12% through a full cycle, which would force a re-rating of the shipbuilding leg's quality.
Explanation of the KRW 1.42T H1 2026 capital surplus increase that occurred with no new shares issued.
reduce_or_exit_evidence: Operating cash flow remaining negative for FY2026 as a whole — this would move external_capital_dependence from INVESTIGATE to FAIL and make REJECT a veto-driven conclusion rather than a score-driven one.
Any further equity raise, which would confirm structural external-capital dependence twelve months after the last one.
Defence backlog declining, not just defence revenue — that would remove the one genuinely strong element of the case.
Marine margin reverting toward the 7.7% FY2025 level as the current backlog vintage delivers.
Borrowings rising above roughly KRW 18T, or the current ratio falling below 1.0.
Any indication that European orders carry offset obligations materially heavier than assumed, transferring value to customer countries.
